messages:
jamie (eng-runtime): noticing a big p99 spike on EU dedicated pool, started ~03:10 UTC. throughput dropped, queueing shot up. KV evictions are crazy high. creating this thread to triage.

sasha (eng-sre): link to the dashboard? any recent placement or quota changes?

jamie (eng-runtime): https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/eu-dedicated — p99 went from ~180ms to 1.8s. quick scrub of metrics: high `kv_cache.evictions/sec` and kernel_selector falling back to slow kernels. logs snapshot:
```
[03:09:58] placement.assign: host=eu-1 pool=dedicated tenants_assigned=118
[03:10:01] placement.assign: host=eu-2 pool=dedicated tenants_assigned=122
[03:10:05] kv_cache.evictions/sec=340 (baseline 12)
[03:10:07] kernel_selector: fallback=slow_quant_kernel model=model-x reason=kv_miss
[03:10:10] request_queue.length=84
```

mike (eng-ml): those eviction numbers explain a lot — when KV cache is thrashing continuous-batching collapses and kernel selector picks an execution path with much higher per-token latency. any recent kernel changes?

jamie (eng-runtime): kernel builds unchanged. I dug into placement service history — a migration merged earlier today. the migration defaulted a quota param oddly. diff below:
```
- per_host_quota: 10
+ per_host_quota: ${MIGRATE_PER_HOST:-100}
```

teri (product): wait, so we accidentally ended up with ~100 tenants per host in eu? that would explain noisy neighbor + cache pressure. who reviewed the migration?

sasha (eng-sre): looks like the CI guard didn't block this because env var was set in the deploy. action plan: 1) scale down tenant assignments back to sane defaults, 2) re-enable evict backoff, 3) rollback migration if needed. I'm about to run placement-fix.sh to reassign.

jamie (eng-runtime): running `curl -XPOST https://placement.service/eu/rebalance -d '{"target_per_host":10}'` now. I'll also throttle incoming allocation requests at the LB.

deploy-bot: Deploy initiated by sasha — placement-service v2.3.7 -> v2.3.6 (rollback)

sasha (eng-sre): rollback in progress. also toggled `kv_cache.evict_backoff=true` on eu pool.

jamie (eng-runtime): quick post-rollback probe: `kv_cache.evictions/sec` dropped to 18 within 3m, p99 is down to ~220ms. still watching for secondary effects.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260312-34 created, severity=sev2, assignees=eng-runtime,eng-sre

mike (eng-ml): follow-ups to prevent recurrence: add CI lint that prevents defaulting quotas from env vars without explicit override, add histogram alert for `kv_cache.evictions/sec > 50`, and add a small canary for placement changes. Also we should run a profiling job to confirm kernel_selector choices post-fix.

teri (product): agreed. I'll open a customer-impact ticket and start drafting the postmortem template. recommend contacting customers in EU dedicated who saw >1s p99.

sasha (eng-sre): noted. I'll also add a temporary placement-safety check in the operator runbook.

jamie (eng-runtime): root cause summary for postmortem: migration script introduced an env-driven default that bumped `per_host_quota` to ~100 in EU, causing tenant co-location to spike, KV cache thrash, kernel selector fallback to slow path, and p99 latency regression. mitigation = rollback + evict backoff + throttled allocations.

sasha (eng-sre): :thumbsup: closing incident when stable for 1h and no regression.

jamie (eng-runtime): closing note will be posted to #postmortems after 24h of stability. thanks everyone.
